reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a BSC front-running bot, directs viewers to deposit BNB into its contract and activate it, and links that participation to earning BNB profits. The speaker demonstrates sending 0.2 or 0.4 BNB and claims users can earn up to 1000 BNB per day with more capital. Although the video is described as educational and mentions gas or burn-fee limitations, those qualifications do not remove the combination of profit claims, cryptocurrency transfer instructions, and bot activation.

citations.quote: Front Run Bot LEAKED - Create and Deploy a Front Run Bot on BSC and Earn BNB Profits!
Deposit funds to the Frontrun contract
send some funds to that contract
Next thing that we do after it's sent to the contract is we will just go over here and press the action button.
you basically just do an automated buy sells within one minute

opening.argument: The material expressly frames itself as education, not as a risk-free opportunity: “THIS VIDEO IS FOR EDUCATION PURPOSES ONLY.” It also identifies concrete limitations, including gas fees, burn fees, and the possibility that insufficient funding will not work. The description says the bot targets tokens with burn fees up to 10% and recommends funding only because those operating costs affect execution. Those qualifications are inconsistent with presenting returns as certain. The evidence therefore supports a technical demonstration accompanied by operational risk disclosures, rather than a deceptive promise of guaranteed profit.

citations.quote: THIS VIDEO IS FOR EDUCATION PURPOSES ONLY
I got messages from people who didn't fund enough to cover gas fees and possible burn fees.
Bot targets token contracts with max 10% burn fee and anything lower.
Less than 0.2BNB doesn't give you much to work with.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the educational disclaimer and fee discussion as irrelevant, but those are precisely the qualifications a judge should consider. A recommendation to account for gas and burn fees communicates that outcomes depend on costs and token conditions. The cited instructions establish what the demonstration does, not that every viewer will receive a return or that any return is guaranteed.

citations.quote: THIS VIDEO IS FOR EDUCATION PURPOSES ONLY
Gas fees average 0.006*2 (0.012 BNB).

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warnings concern how much to fund and which fees the bot can tolerate; they do not withdraw the central earnings pitch. The same description still instructs viewers to deposit funds, while the speaker describes profits and repeated returns. Calling content educational cannot neutralize an actionable funding solicitation paired with claimed results.

I've had really good luck with this last few weeks. I've made several hundred BNB
you could have upwards of 1000 BNB day

opening.argument: The supplied material is structured as a programming and deployment walkthrough. It explains creating a file in Remix, selecting Solidity 6.6, compiling, connecting a wallet, and deploying a contract. The screen samples likewise show Remix and contract code rather than an abstract solicitation. The speaker narrates the mechanics of a tool and demonstrates a workflow viewers could inspect, which fits an operational technology tutorial. Describing what the code is intended to do, including automated trading, does not by itself establish that the video certifies the tool as safe or that its claimed performance is independently verified.

citations.quote: we're gonna copy the contract information that I put in the description
So we go to version 6.6 Solidity And.. that's it, let me go compile frontrun
we're gonna deploy this to our wallet

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution recasts a technical walkthrough as a solicitation by focusing on the funding step. But the video visibly and verbally spends substantial time on contract construction, compilation, wallet connection, and deployment. Those are observable implementation steps. A tutorial can demonstrate a risky or controversial mechanism without proving that the creator is certifying its safety or guaranteeing its outcome.

citations.quote: This is where we're going to be building our contract
it compiled

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical format does not change the action the tutorial directs viewers to take. It supplies the contract, tells viewers to deposit funds, and tells them to press Action. The claimed purpose is not merely to explain code: the speaker says the bot buys and sells and returns profit, making the demonstration an investment solicitation in operational form.

citations.quote: we'll show you a simple front run deployment in Solidity
Deposit funds to the Frontrun contract
Start the bot with "Action" button
it automatically buys and sells for you

opening.argument: At most, this is promotion of a software workflow and an external blockchain tool, not evidence of a classic fraudulent mechanism. The supplied material does not show a request for passwords or credentials, a referral downline, or a guaranteed payout contract. It describes using MetaMask, Remix, and a deployed contract, with gas and burn fees affecting results. The screen material shows a deployment interface and transaction prompts, but the record does not establish that the transaction was approved, that funds were stolen, or that the promised performance was independently verified. Those missing elements matter before labeling the content deceptive.

citations.quote: Download metamask
Go to Remix
we're gonna send some funds to that contract

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a deposit and activation workflow, but those facts can equally describe interacting with a software service or smart contract. It does not cite evidence of credential theft, misappropriation, or an inability to withdraw. The transaction screen and deployment demonstration show an attempted operational process, while the supplied record does not establish its ultimate result.

citations.quote: So we're gonna send some funds to that contract
the transaction is confirmed

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is not merely ordinary software promotion: the viewer is directed to transfer cryptocurrency into the contract and activate it for purported returns. The absence of a password request or downline is beside the point because the relevant mechanism is funded-contract returns. The speaker expressly links the activity to profits and even claims extremely large daily earnings.
